title: Dyeing with sweet woodruff
subtitle: A pale yellow-green on alum-mordanted wool from this shade-loving herb
excerpt: Sweet woodruff gives a soft yellow-green on alum-mordanted wool. Gather the fresh herb in flower in late spring and use it fresh or dried. The colour is muted and light-fast on wool; it makes a good base for overdyeing with woad to produce soft blue-greens.
sourceNotes: Pellew, Dyes and Dyeing (1913), Internet Archive. Pellew lists sweet woodruff among the plant materials giving yellow-green shades on mordanted wool. Hummel, The Dyeing of Textile Fabrics (1885), Internet Archive, provides the alum mordant procedure.

glossaryTerms.definition: A metallic salt that bonds to wool fibre and provides attachment sites for plant dye molecules, improving colour fastness and depth.
Potassium aluminium sulphate, the standard beginner mordant for wool. It produces warm, clear colours and is the safest mordant for home use.
Resistant to fading when exposed to light. Natural dyes vary greatly in light-fastness; alum-mordanted plant yellows are moderately light-fast.

content.text: Sweet woodruff gives a pale yellow-green on
wool. The colour is soft and muted: not a strong yellow but a greenish-cream that reads well as a natural plant colour. It is moderately

on wool, better than many plant yellows, and combines well with a woad overdye to produce blue-green shades. The whole above-ground plant gives the most colour; gather it in flower in late May and June.

attrs.title: Mordant safety
attrs.body: Dye-pot work outdoors or in a ventilated kitchen. Dedicated pot and utensils only. Gloves and apron. Alum bath can compost after use.

attrs.title: Dye-plant cross-reference
attrs.body: Sweet woodruff (Galium odoratum) is a shade-tolerant ground-cover herb. See the Garden tutorial on growing sweet woodruff for harvest guidance.

items.name: Fresh sweet woodruff (whole plant above ground)
items.qty: 2 to 3 times the dry weight of fibre being dyed

items.name: Alum mordant (potassium alum)
items.qty: 15% of the dry weight of fibre

items.name: Dedicated stainless steel or enamelled dye-pot

content.text: Dissolve alum in a small amount of hot water and add to the dye-pot filled with enough warm water to cover the fibre freely. Pre-wet the wool in warm water for 20 minutes. Enter the wool into the mordant bath at 40°C, raise the temperature slowly to 80°C over 30 minutes, hold at 80°C for 45 minutes. Lower the temperature slowly and either remove the fibre for immediate dyeing or leave it in the cooling mordant bath overnight.
Simmer the sweet woodruff plant material in water at 80°C for 45 to 60 minutes. Strain out the plant material and return the dye liquor to the pot. The bath will be a pale yellow-green colour.

Enter the mordanted fibre into the dye bath at 40°C. Raise slowly to 80°C and hold for 45 to 60 minutes, turning the fibre occasionally. The colour develops gradually; it will be paler than expected when wet. Lower the temperature, leave the fibre in the cooling bath for another 30 minutes, then remove, rinse in warm water, and dry in shade.

An iron after-bath shifts the yellow-green toward olive-green and slightly deepens the colour. Add a small amount of dissolved iron mordant to a fresh warm water bath, enter the dyed fibre, hold at 60°C for 15 minutes, then rinse well. The colour shift is immediate and irreversible; add iron in small increments to avoid greying the colour too much.

items.problem: The colour is very pale, barely visible
items.cause: Insufficient plant material relative to fibre weight, or the dye-bath was not hot enough to extract the colour fully
items.fix: Use at least twice the dry plant weight relative to fibre weight. Extract at a full 80°C. Sweet woodruff is a mild dye plant; a pale result is normal at lower plant-to-fibre ratios.

items.problem: The colour faded noticeably after the first washing
items.cause: The mordant proportion was too low or the mordant bath was not held at temperature long enough to bond the alum to the fibre
items.fix: Re-mordant in a fresh alum bath at 15% weight-of-fibre, holding at 80°C for the full 45 minutes. A properly mordanted yellow on sweet woodruff should not fade significantly in a normal handwash.
